references.text: The immediate context describing how the children of Israel broke camp when the cloud lifted from the tabernacle and set up camp when the cloud stopped.
Summarizes the principle that the Israelites followed the Lord's command through the cloud, both when they set up camp and when they broke camp.
The first example of the cloud lifting from the tabernacle of the testimony and the Israelites breaking camp from the wilderness of Sinai.
The original description of the cloud over the tabernacle that led the journeys of the children of Israel.
Confirms that the Lord led the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord went before them in fire at night and in a cloud by day to show them the way.
Nehemiah refers to God's faithfulness when the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire led the Israelites through the wilderness.
The psalm describes how God led the people with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night long.
Refers to God's guidance through the cloud as a covering and the fire as light at night.
Paul mentions that the fathers were all under the cloud, pointing back to God's guidance of Israel in the wilderness.
